name: Griffin Mission One
operator: Astrobotic (US, commercial; renamed Voyager Lunar Systems after Voyager Technologies' acquisition closed Jul 13, 2026)
short_status: Flight lander built, unveiled Jun 15, 2026, and finished acceptance testing at NASA JPL (NASA and Voyager, Oct 13, 2026); now back in Pittsburgh for final assembly before shipment to Cape Canaveral, with a Falcon Heavy launch targeted for late 2026 (as of Nov 2, 2026).

facts.label: Organisations
facts.value: Astrobotic (US, commercial; renamed Voyager Lunar Systems after Voyager Technologies' acquisition closed Jul 13, 2026)

facts.label: Status (as of Nov 2, 2026)
facts.value: Acceptance testing at NASA JPL complete (NASA and Voyager, 13 Oct 2026): mass properties, electromagnetic, vibration and acoustic tests from July, then about two weeks in JPL's 25-Foot Space Simulator thermal vacuum chamber. The lander has returned to Voyager Lunar Systems' Pittsburgh facility for final assembly and launch-readiness work before shipment to Cape Canaveral. Launch targeted for late 2026 (Voyager, 13 Oct 2026; NASA launch schedule, updated 14 Oct 2026), no earlier than November per NASA's Moon Base program manager (15 Sep 2026)

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: Targeted for late 2026, no earlier than November (as of November 2026), SpaceX Falcon Heavy from LC-39A, Kennedy Space Center

facts.label: Landing target
facts.value: Mons Mouton, the flat-topped mountain near Nobile crater at the lunar south pole; the VIPER-era site region, with no specific point published (as of October 2026)

facts.label: Lander
facts.value: About 4.5 m wide and 2.0 m tall, 625 kg payload capacity to the surface, seven main engines, four attitude-thruster clusters, 100 m landing accuracy target

facts.label: Primary payload
facts.value: Astrolab's FLIP rover, 500 kg, announced 5 February 2025; matures tires, batteries, avionics and software for Astrolab's larger FLEX vehicle

facts.label: NASA instruments on FLIP
facts.value: Five NASA payloads by NASA's own August 2026 count, among them the METAL multicolor camera and radiometer, a laser retroreflector array, a lunar dust sensor, and a lidar demonstration for 3D surface mapping; the sources that give the count do not name the fifth

facts.label: Full manifest
facts.value: 10 payloads from six countries, including BEACON (CubeRover autonomy demo with Canada's Mission Control), ESA's LandCam-X landing camera, and a Nanofiche nickel micro-archive

facts.label: CLPS task order
facts.value: $199.5 million awarded 11 June 2020 (TO 20A) to deliver NASA's VIPER rover to the lunar south pole

facts.label: VIPER removed
facts.value: 17 July 2024: NASA ended the VIPER project over cost growth; Griffin-1 continued under its contract as a flight demonstration of the lander and its engines, with NASA retaining the task order (about $323 million by then)

facts.label: VIPER's second life
facts.value: 19 September 2025: NASA awarded Blue Origin a task order with a total potential value of $190 million to deliver VIPER on a Blue Moon MK1 lander, targeted for late 2027 (as of that announcement)

facts.label: Moon Base II designation
facts.value: 26 May 2026: NASA renamed its first three upcoming CLPS-lineage landers Moon Base I (Blue Moon MK1 Endurance), II (Griffin-1) and III (IM-3 Trinity); Griffin-1 delivers more than 1,100 pounds of cargo

facts.label: Ownership
facts.value: Voyager Technologies' acquisition of Astrobotic, announced 2 June 2026, closed 13 July 2026 ($162 million in cash and stock, up to $129 million in earnouts, $9 million debt assumed); the company is now Voyager Lunar Systems, still led by John Thornton

timeline: CLPS task order awarded: $199.5 million to deliver NASA's VIPER rover to the lunar south pole
VIPER landing zone announced: the mountainous area west of Nobile crater, officially named Mons Mouton in 2022
VIPER pulled from Griffin: NASA ends the VIPER project; Griffin-1 continues as a flight demonstration of the lander and its engines
FLIP named primary payload: Astrolab's 500 kg rover replaces the planned mass simulator
VIPER reassigned to Blue Origin: task order with a total potential value of $190 million to deliver the rover on Blue Moon MK1, targeted late 2027
Oct 2025
Launch slips to mid-2026: target moves from late 2025 to NET July 2026
Designated Moon Base II: NASA names its first three Moon Base lander missions
Flight lander unveiled at the Moonshot Museum in Pittsburgh, then shipped to JPL for environmental testing
Voyager acquisition closes: Astrobotic becomes Voyager Lunar Systems
NASA and Voyager announce that Griffin-1 finished acceptance testing at NASA JPL; the lander is back in Pittsburgh for final assembly before shipment to Cape Canaveral
Targeted late 2026
Launch, no earlier than November 2026, on Falcon Heavy from KSC LC-39A (as of Nov 2026)
NET late 2026
Landing attempt at the Mons Mouton area near Nobile crater, a few days after launch (as of Nov 2026)
